# GenAI Usage (How / Failure / Tradeoff)

[← Amazon](../README.md) · [Every Amazon question](../../amazon.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/bq-genai-usage)

`ai-tools`

---

## Preparation Requirements

- Develop 2–3 specific GenAI experiences in STAR format—situation, task, action, and result—with at least one positive outcome and one failure or tradeoff.
- Be prepared to justify the model selection (Claude, GPT, or an internal model), the prompting approach (chain-of-thought, retrieval, or agent), and the result using numbers.
- Applied Scientist and MLE candidates should also prepare examples involving agent construction, including multiple turns, context overflow, and tool use.

## Sample Questions

Prompts reported from recent interview loops include:

- “Describe a situation in which you used GenAI.”
- “Tell me about a GenAI project or attempt that failed.”
- “Explain a time when an AI system produced an incorrect answer—how did you identify it, and how did you respond?”
- “What role does AI play in your everyday work?”
- “How would you build a multi-turn agent, and what would you do when its context becomes too large?”
- “How would you design the architecture for an AI chatbot?”

## Interview Notes

- Follow-up questioning is typically intense, so anticipate at least two layers of “why” and “what would you change?”
- General statements such as “I used ChatGPT for summaries” tend to perform poorly; include measurable effects such as latency, accuracy, or time saved.
- AS and MLE candidates should incorporate agent, multi-turn, and context-management terminology, while SDE candidates may remain focused on the application layer.
- An interviewer generally covers 1–3 Leadership Principles and asks 2–3 behavioral questions during the slot; plan for 10–15 minutes of repeated follow-ups on one story instead of quick shifts between subjects.
- AI tools cannot be used during the live interview; this GenAI behavioral round concerns your previous use of such tools, not a request to demonstrate one on screen.
- In AS and MLE interviews, state agent-design terms directly—such as the tool-use loop, context-window management, and an evaluation harness—because broad answers like “I prompted the model” regularly perform worse.

## Preparation Plan

- Draft three GenAI STAR stories covering success, failure, and tradeoff, and remember the metric that concludes each one.
- Rehearse the “what would you do differently?” portion for every story, since Amazon Leadership Principles value an iterative mindset.
- For technical examples, prepare at least one agent or multi-turn case that clearly explains how context is managed.
